refnamediv.refpurpose: Open Internet or Unix domain socket connection

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
address
Address to the socket to connect to.
error_code
Will be set to the system level error number if connection fails.
error_message
Will be set to the system level error message if the connection fails.
timeout
Number of seconds until the connect() system call should timeout. By default, default_socket_timeout is used. As of PHP 8.1.0, a negative value is the same as &null;; before, the call did not wait for any limit of its own. With 0, the call fails at once with error 110 unless the connection is established instantly. For ssl:// and tls:// addresses, the same value also bounds the TLS handshake.
This parameter only applies when not making asynchronous connection attempts.
To set a timeout for reading/writing data over the socket, use the stream_set_timeout, as the timeout only applies while making connecting the socket.
flags
Bitmask field which may be set to any combination of connection flags. Currently the select of connection flags is limited to STREAM_CLIENT_CONNECT (default), STREAM_CLIENT_ASYNC_CONNECT and STREAM_CLIENT_PERSISTENT.
With STREAM_CLIENT_ASYNC_CONNECT on a tcp:// address, a stream is returned immediately, even if the connection is refused, with error_code 0 and an empty error_message: the failure only appears later, as a failed write or an end of file. The flag does not make an ssl:// connection asynchronous: the call blocks during the handshake, up to timeout, and then fails.
context
A valid context resource created with stream_context_create.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
On success a stream resource is returned which may be used together with the other file functions (such as fgets, fwrite, fclose, and feof), &false; on failure.

&reftitle.seealso;
